title: What If an Oreshnik Nuke Hit Germany From Belarus?
description:
What would a nuclear Oreshnik missile launched from Belarus do to Germany, and how many minutes of warning would Europe get?

A simulated launch from eastern Belarus reaches Ramstein Air Base in about 8 minutes, and every European capital sits inside 6 to 9 minutes in our model: this video shows the flight clock, then the blast rings.

Eighteen minutes past three in the morning, western Germany: a nuclear weapon bursts over Ramstein Air Base. Eight minutes earlier, a road-mobile launcher stopped in a forest in Belarus. Radars see a ballistic track, and nobody can tell what is on top of it. How many minutes does Europe get, and what can anyone do with them?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY. The launch point, target, warhead and yield are our choices, a scenario, not a forecast and not a known Russian plan, and we set no date.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:42 The missile that flew fifteen minutes
2:51 The last time Europe had minutes
4:49 The launch
6:14 Minute by minute
8:14 One warhead, ring by ring
9:18 The day after

Key sources

- Al Jazeera, Russia deploys Oreshnik missiles in Belarus (2025-12-31): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/31/russia-deploys-hypersonic-oreshnik-missiles-in-belarus-amid-europe-tensions
- Arms Control Association, the INF Treaty at a glance: https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/inftreaty
- Arms Control Association, Russia cancels its intermediate-range missile moratorium: https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2025-09/russia-cancels-intermediate-range-missile-moratorium
- Arms Control Association, New START expires: https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2026-03/news/new-start-expires-us-urges-modernized-treaty

Flight times, blast and burn figures: our scenario engine (Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons, 1977, calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein). The launch point and yield are simulation choices.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the launch point, warhead, yield, targets and timing are ours.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Thumbnail backgrounds are AI-generated. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
